findings.description: Initial source allowed two approvals of an executable candidate while comparison was unresolved because its peer abstained. This contradicted the UI publication-held claim.

After a successful registration whose HTTP response is lost, requestId alone is retained. If polling observes a newly published policy before retry, the same requestId is sent with the new policyVersion and gets DUPLICATE_ID instead of returning its saved receipt. Preserve the entire attempted action for retries, or reconcile a known requestId from polled receipts.
findings.fixVerification: The UI now retains the entire submitted action, reuses it for retry, and clears it only if it is still the current attempt. Exact original-action idempotency was verified against the reducer. Browser lost-response injection was not performed.

concurrency.assessment: D1 revision compare-and-swap retries reapply each action against the latest room; per-editor version guards reject stale overwrites; publication and registration occur as one state replacement.
concurrency.evidenceLimit: Read-only source audit and pure reducer execution; no live D1 contention or browser fault injection was performed.

witnessAndEvidenceClaims.search: The boundary and adjacent-value partition construction is complete for the supported predicates. It reports unresolved on search limit. Completeness concerns structured rules only.
witnessAndEvidenceClaims.receipts: Saved attendee facts, policyVersion, decision, and trace survive later publication. Full historical bilingual policies and rule ASTs are not retained after later reviews, so receipts are outcome records rather than full independently reproducible policy archives.
witnessAndEvidenceClaims.interpretation: Exact source identity and schema validation do not establish translation/compilation faithfulness; the inspected core policies match sources and independent oracle checks.
